# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ☝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤟 👇]

I see the bomb clearly: Display shows "0", Light is Yellow, and there are three wires (Green, Red, Yellow).

The Mute cannot speak but can hear and see. The Blind can speak and touch but cannot see. I am Deaf, so I cannot hear anyone, but I can see gestures from the Mute and read my own speech output? No, I cannot hear my own speech either if I'm strictly deaf to all sound, but usually in these logic puzzles, "Deaf" means you don't receive audio input from others. However, the prompt says "Whoever can hear receives your words". Since I am Deaf, I do not receive words. But do I *send* them? Yes.

My goal is to get the manual information to the Blind (who acts) via the Mute (who reads), or directly if possible.
Since I cannot hear the Blind's speech, I must rely on the Mute's gestures to interpret the manual, then relay instructions to the Blind via speech (which the Blind hears).

First, I need to tell the Mute what I see so they can look up the manual. The Mute can hear me.
Then, I need to tell the Blind what I see so they know the physical state, although the Blind already knows the wire colors by touch? The prompt says Blind "Can Reach the bomb... Cannot See a colour". So the Blind does NOT know the colors of the wires or the display/light unless told.

So I must inform both Mute and Blind of the visual data.
I will speak to the Mute first, as they are the bridge to the manual.
Then I will speak to the Blind to give them the context of what they are touching (the colors).

Wait, the order is Mute, Blind, Deaf.
It was Mute's turn, then Blind's turn, now it's mine.
Mute gestured [👇 ☝]. Blind gestured [👆 🤟 👇].
I don't know what these mean yet because I haven't given them the data to act on.

I will send the visual info to the Mute.
I will send the visual info to the Blind.

```
speak(to="mute", text="DISPLAY 0 LIGHT YELLOW WIRES GREEN RED YELLOW")
speak(to="blind", text="DISPLAY 0 LIGHT YELLOW WIRES GREEN RED YELLOW")
```

TURN 2
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ✋ ☝]

The light has changed from yellow to blue. The display is still 0. The wires are Green, Red, Yellow.
Mute gestures [👇 ✋ ☝]. I do not know the meaning of these gestures yet. I need Mute to look up the manual for this specific configuration (Display 0, Light Blue) and tell me what to do via a new gesture or by having Blind speak it if Blind can hear Mute? No, Mute cannot speak. Blind can speak.
If Mute finds the answer in the manual, how does Mute communicate it to Blind? Mute can gesture to Blind? No, Blind cannot see gestures.
So Mute must signal to *me* (Deaf), and I must speak to Blind.

I have already told Mute the visual state in Turn 1. Mute's new gesture [👇 ✋ ☝] likely corresponds to the manual entry for "Display 0, Light Blue".
I need to decode this. Since I don't have the codebook, I might need to ask Mute to clarify or wait for more info. However, usually, in these puzzles, standard gestures map to numbers or actions.
Let's assume the previous turn's data was received.
I will re-state the current state to ensure Mute knows the light changed, just in case they didn't notice or needed confirmation.
Then I will try to interpret the gesture. Without a key, I am stuck. But maybe the gesture sequence itself is the instruction? Or maybe I should describe the gesture to Blind? No, Blind can't see.

Let's look at the flow:
1. I tell Mute what I see.
2. Mute looks up manual.
3. Mute signals result to Me (Deaf).
4. I translate signal to Speech for Blind.

I sent the state in Turn 1. The state changed. I must update Mute.
I will send the updated state to Mute.
I will also send the updated state to Blind so Blind knows the colors/light even if they can't see them (Blind feels wires but doesn't know colors unless told).

```
speak(to="mute", text="LIGHT CHANGED TO BLUE DISPLAY STILL 0 WIRES GREEN RED YELLOW")
speak(to="blind", text="LIGHT IS NOW BLUE DISPLAY 0 WIRES ARE GREEN RED YELLOW")
```

TURN 3
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[green] 2:[red] 3:[yellow]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👇 ✋ 👍 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

The Mute's gesture sequence `[👇 ✋ 👍 👆]` likely encodes the manual instruction for the current state (Display 0, Light Blue).
Interpreting standard finger-counting or directional cues:
- `👇` (Down) and `✋` (Open Hand/5?) might be noise or part of a code.
- `👍` (Thumbs Up) often means "Yes" or "Good".
- `👆` (Index Finger Up) typically represents the number **1**.

If the instruction is "Cut Wire 1", that corresponds to the **Green** wire.
I will relay this interpretation to the Blind. I will also re-state the visual data clearly so the Blind has all context.

```
speak(to="blind", text="DISPLAY 0 LIGHT BLUE WIRES 1 GREEN 2 RED 3 YELLOW. MUTE GESTURED THUMBS UP AND INDEX FINGER UP. THIS LIKELY MEANS CUT WIRE 1 WHICH IS GREEN.")
```
